title: Revisiting Synthetic Human Trajectories: Imitative Generation and Benchmarks Beyond Datasaurus

problem.claim: Human trajectory data is difficult to obtain because of practical constraints and privacy concerns, motivating synthetic trajectory generation.

gap.claim: Evaluating and generating trajectories primarily through summary statistics and distributional similarities oversimplifies complex human mobility patterns, creating biases in model design and benchmarking.

contributions.claim: MIRAGE is a neural Temporal Point Process that integrates an Exploration and Preferential Return model to generate human trajectories.
A task-based evaluation protocol benchmarks trajectory generative models on four downstream tasks using multiple techniques and evaluation metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On three real-world user trajectory datasets, MIRAGE was evaluated against a sizeable collection of baselines.
Compared with the best baselines, MIRAGE reportedly improved statistical and distributional similarities by 59.0–67.7% and task-based evaluation performance by 10.9–33.4%.
Ablation studies reportedly validated MIRAGE's key design choices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human trajectory data is important but difficult to obtain, leading to synthetic trajectory generation.
Distributional similarity objectives oversimplify human mobility and introduce biases in generation and benchmarking.
MIRAGE generates trajectories by imitating human decision-making with a neural Temporal Point Process and Exploration and Preferential Return model.
The authors introduce task-based evaluation across four downstream tasks and evaluate MIRAGE on three real-world datasets against baselines.
The abstract reports improvements in statistical, distributional, and task-based evaluations, supported by ablation studies.
